title: Unequal load fanout during inter-region failover — incident analysis and action playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-02-20 at ~02:12 UTC we experienced a multi-region failover that resulted in an uneven fanout of traffic to the us-west-2 serving pool. The sudden imbalance exceeded soft concurrency targets on a subset of serving nodes, leading to an SLO miss for 99th-token-latency and a visible increase in error rates for hosted API customers. Circuit breakers in the serving proxy did not trigger early enough due to stale thresholds; automatic load-shedding rules were not applied because the regional traffic policy did not map to the new allocation. This ticket captures the incident analysis, immediate mitigations that were applied, and a playbook of follow-up action items to reduce recurrence risk.
timeline: 2026-02-20T02:12:00Z - Primary region (us-east-1) reported intermittent infra network degradation; traffic was routed to failover policy.
2026-02-20T02:13:40Z - Traffic steering service pushed config to route 87% of traffic to us-west-2 (expected 50%).
2026-02-20T02:15:00Z - Serving pool us-west-2 saw sustained 2.3x normal qps for ~4 minutes; tail latency increased and error rate rose from 0.2% to 4.8%.
2026-02-20T02:16:30Z - First automated circuit-breaker open event observed but thresholds were too permissive; many connections kept consuming KV cache resources.
2026-02-20T02:18:00Z - On-call shifted manual traffic split to 60/40 and increased autoscaler target; partial recovery after 90s.
2026-02-20T02:30:00Z - SLO window recorded 99th-token-latency breach for 12 consecutive minutes. Incident declared P1 and page routed to reliability team.
2026-02-20T03:05:00Z - Hotfix deployed to routing service to enforce per-region cap and enabled conservative circuit-breaker policy; full recovery by 03:12 UTC.
root_cause: Routing service bug: a race condition in the roll-forward logic allowed an outdated weight map to be applied; resulting fanout heavily favored us-west-2.
Circuit breaker configuration drift: thresholds were calibrated for homogenous load patterns and did not account for abrupt fanout spikes (static thresholds).
Load-shedding policy mismatch: emergency shedding was keyed by route ID, but failover used a temporary route alias that bypassed shedding rules.
mitigations: Immediate: manual traffic rebalancing to 60/40 and increased the replica count in us-west-2 to absorb burst.
Hotfix: patched routing service to remove race and added an atomic swap for weight maps (deployed 2026-02-20 02:58 UTC).
Fallback: enabled conservative circuit-breaker mode globally to favor early short-circuiting for small-number-of-connections overloads.
action_items: Miguel Ortega - Implement adaptive circuit-breaker thresholds (windowed latency + capacity signal) and rollout as opt-in feature - due 2026-04-02 - status: In Progress
Sana Liu - Add route-alias mapping into load-shedding rules and backfill existing aliases across regions - due 2026-03-26 - status: Todo

Corey Nguyen - Add unit+integration tests for routing weight swap (cover race case) and add a canary that validates atomicity before rollout - due 2026-03-10 - status: Done (PR merged: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2134)
Reliability Team - Create synthetic inter-region failover smoke tests that run in CI nightly and simulate 2x traffic fanout - due 2026-03-19 - status: In Progress
Platform - Ship a dashboard tile that surfaces 'region fanout delta' and alerts when any region exceeds expected share by >30% for 1 minute - due 2026-03-12 - status: In Review
Security - Perform risk review for routing hotfix and ensure no secret or KMS access patterns were altered - due 2026-03-05 - status: Done
